title: How Toilets Evolved
upload_title: How Toilets Evolved 🚽 From a Hole in the Ground to One Push #shorts #engineering

beats.text: 5,000 years ago, there was no toilet.
The problem? People went out in the open. Waste washed into rivers, and disease spread fast.
The first fix: dig a pit, and keep waste underground.
But pits filled up, and they stank.
The Romans built stone seats over running water, to wash waste away.
In 1596, John Harington built a toilet that flushed, with a water tank above.
But the open pipe let sewer smells rise straight back up.
In 1775, Alexander Cumming bent the pipe into an S. Trapped water blocks the smell.
Then cities built huge sewers, to carry waste far from homes.
And today, one push sends it all away.
Treatment plants clean the water, and return it to rivers.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
